text:
Dmitri Simashev came to the NHL with a defensive reputation and 1 point in 28 games last season. This season he has 4 goals in 22, and our wins added measure, which weighs goals by how much they swung the game, ranks him 90th of 541 skaters. Several of those goals came at moments that mattered.

His minutes say Utah trusts him more each week: 17.3 a night over the last ten games, with four games over 19 minutes. A team video put it simply: "Dmitri Simashev Joins Odd-Man Rush."

Our numbers expect some cooling. He's shooting 17.4% against a talent range centred near 6.7%, so the goal pace is the luck part. The process is mixed: Utah has been nearly ten points worse in expected goal share (chance quality) at five on five with him on than off. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small sample of 7 games, had 44% of his shots coming off the rush and half his exits leaving the zone with possession.

The sixth overall pick in 2023, taken between David Reinbacher and Matvei Michkov, is 21. The goals are a bonus; the minutes are the story.
